html:
The aflaj (singular falaj) are the water channels of Oman, which carry groundwater or spring water by gravity, often through tunnels, to villages and date gardens. Some go back to the Iron Age, about 3,000 years ago.

Like the qanats of Iran, they let people farm in a dry land. Thousands still work. Water is shared out by time, measured once by sundials and the stars, and the shares are owned, sold and inherited.

The falaj shaped the Omani village, its fort, its mosque and its communal rules. Five aflaj became a World Heritage Site in 2006. See also the Al Ain oasis and Nizwa.
